clue.text: Little time to use art form in garden tool

parts.note: a sec, short for second, is a little time

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it anew, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone takes a moment to fashion art from the tools in their garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' looks like a noun (an art form) but is the anagram signal, turning 'use art' into ATEURS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are pruning shears, a standard cutting implement used by gardeners on shrubs and roses.

clue.text: See 21
See 21
Bird (cock) takes small part

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
a cock is a male bird, so a he

explanation.surface: A cockbird picks up a little piece of food.
explanation.walkthrough: '(cock)' looks like more about the bird, but it gives HE, the male.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth was the traditional portion paid to the church, a small share of produce.

clue.text: Tune quality's different

indicators.note: the 's stands for has: the clue words have the answer within them

explanation.surface: A remark that a tune's quality varies.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'Tune quality', with the 's read as 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are not equal in size or amount are different from each other.

clue.text: Fish and horse entertaining theatrical company with play

parts.note: a school is a group of fish

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a foal is a young horse
RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company
and means together with

explanation.surface: An angler and a horse play host to touring actors putting on a show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' looks like amusing but means holding inside. The whole is Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal; RSC is the Royal Shakespeare Company.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a famous eighteenth-century stage comedy by Richard Brinsley Sheridan.

clue.text: Oriental drink could be 9's

definitions.meaning: the entry at 9 is HEAVEN, and the exclamation is for heaven's ___

explanation.surface: A Japanese drink might be heavenly.
explanation.definitionFit: The rice wine of Japan, and the word completing the exclamation for heaven's ___.

clue.text: See 5
Waterway king that's all confused about vessel

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another
confused means mixed up, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a can is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A muddled monarch fusses about a boat on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns 'all' into LAL; 'about' wraps it round the vessel. The canal crosses northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The canal across Schleswig-Holstein linking the North Sea and Baltic is a man-made waterway.

clue.text: Theatrical skill slips aside with ready wit

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
art means skill
E.E. is errors excepted: slips set aside

explanation.surface: An actor's craft lets mistakes go by thanks to quick improvisation.
explanation.walkthrough: E.E., 'errors excepted', is an old formula on invoices: slips (errors) set aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick witty retorts in conversation are a display of ready wit.

clue.text: Pull with pole — it's bliss

parts.note: to heave is to pull hard
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Hauling on a pole turns out to be pure joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise stands for a state of supreme happiness, so it is a synonym for bliss.

clue.text: Come out with second vehicle

parts.note: a trike is a three-wheeled cycle

explanation.surface: Someone emerges with another car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come out' is workers going on a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers who come out stop work in protest, which is to walk out on industrial action.

clue.text: Water for the city in the country, not down below

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
a pond is a body of water
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Supplying water to the town from the countryside, while staying above decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the country holding the rest. EC is the postal district of the City, London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, being above on the deck is the opposite of being down below.

clue.text: French appeal as from the heart for nervous affliction in play

parts.words: French appeal as from the heart
parts.note: cri is the French for cry, as in cri de coeur, a heartfelt appeal
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: A heartfelt French plea for help with a nervous condition during a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is Sheridan's The Critic; the article is dropped to fit the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a satirical stage farce by Sheridan about theatre reviewers.

clue.text: One of 8 (where 3 is 19) keeps Walter, a faller

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: in the counting song Green Grow the Rushes, O, three are the rivals and eight the April rainers
Wat is a short form of Walter, as in Wat Tyler

explanation.surface: A cryptic numbered reference holds onto a man named Walter who takes a tumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 and 3 are not grid numbers but lines of the counting song, where 'three, three, the rivals' fixes which song; 'keeps' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from showers literally falls from the sky, so it is wittily called a faller.

clue.text: Cricket captain, watched at Lords, re-settled

indicators.note: re-settled means arranged afresh, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An England captain was watched at Lord's, then moved home.
explanation.walkthrough: The prefix 're' of 're-settled' is fodder; 'settled' is the anagram signal. She captained England's women's cricket team.
explanation.definitionFit: She was the long-serving captain of the England women's cricket side.

clue.text: Distance of China cat from safety measure

parts.note: the li is a Chinese unit of distance
a feline is a member of the cat family

explanation.surface: How far a china cat is from a safety device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain qualifying the cat; it is the country owning the LI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope thrown to someone in difficulty, or any crucial support, is a measure for safety.

clue.text: Make grooves for people as a diversion from river

parts.note: to mill is to cut grooves, as on the edge of a coin
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Folk carve channels as a distraction by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diversion' looks like entertainment; it is water diverted to drive a mill wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the channel carrying water diverted from a stream to turn a waterwheel.

clue.text: Oil producer from the southeast coming in with wrinkles

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: lined means wrinkled
SE is the abbreviation for southeast

explanation.surface: Someone arrives from the southeast with a weathered face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' signals the compass point entering the word for wrinkled.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax seed is pressed to produce an oil used in paints and on cricket bats.

clue.text: See 14
Competes with 5, 6 and 12?

definitions.meaning: the plays at 5, 6 and 12 are by Sheridan, as is this one, so the question points to a fellow comedy

explanation.surface: Something challenges a few numbered entries.
explanation.walkthrough: The plays at 5/6 and 12 are by Sheridan, and so is this comedy; their article is dropped to fit the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Opponents are those who contend with one another, and The Rivals is Sheridan's best-known comedy besides.

clue.text: Capitally protected from pain — sixpence covers it

indicators.note: covers means goes over, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals and D the old abbreviation for pence, from denarius
a sore is a painful affliction

explanation.surface: Head guarded from hurt, with a sixpence on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covers' has the sixpence wrapped round the pain. 'Capitally' means at the head, the capital part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet with a face guard protects the head, the capital part of the body.

clue.text: Society success is radiant: we portray a profusion of song

parts.note: a win is a success
to glow is to be radiant
taken as written
to etch is to portray or depict
a riot is a profusion, as in a riot of colour

explanation.surface: A glittering social triumph: performers depicting abundant music.
explanation.walkthrough: A long charade split over three lights. It is the spiritual sung by English rugby crowds.
explanation.definitionFit: This African-American spiritual is a song, now the anthem of England's rugby fans.

clue.text: Diss in Suffolk? Not much of it, officer

indicators.note: only a small part of the county name is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: Lt is a lieutenant

explanation.surface: A slur in East Anglia, mocking a modest officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a town in Suffolk, an English county, so the surface reads as geography; 'Not much of it' keeps SU.
explanation.definitionFit: To diss is slang for to disrespect someone, so it means to offend or abuse.

clue.text: Porter with line distorted becomes gatecrasher

indicators.note: distorted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doorman with a bent queue lets in an uninvited guest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distorted' rearranges PORTER and LINE together.
explanation.definitionFit: An intruder who pushes in where not invited is a gatecrasher.

clue.text: See 22
Popular acceptance of disturbed rest — and the rest embarrassed?

indicators.note: disturbed means upset, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
embarrassed people turn red

explanation.surface: Uneasy sleep, and everyone else blushing, as a matter of public standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges REST into STRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Credibility among fashionable young people is popular acceptance.

clue.text: Top performer accepts role reversal using pedals

indicators.note: reversal says the whole assembly is read backwards
accepts means takes in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a star is a top performer
a part is a role

explanation.surface: A leading actor takes on a role swap with bicycle parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts PART in STAR for SPARTTAR; 'reversal' reads it backwards. 'Role reversal' looks like one phrase, but only 'reversal' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat-traps are toothed metal cycle pedals, named for their look.

clue.text: See 24
No problem with corollary to 1960s' film

parts.note: easy means no trouble
a rider is a corollary or addition

explanation.surface: No difficulty with a consequence of a sixties movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 road movie starring Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper.
